title: Pedal Bs 1 — three-note bass reconstruction
method: Hardware-only spectral inspection identifies low sine plateaus near 87, 32.3 and 38.5 Hz with Super Saw families roughly one octave above. The published Upper tone octave shift −1 plus WIDE-off sine coarse −12 produces a net −24-semitone sine, while Super Saw coarse 0 gives net −12. These families map to played MIDI 65, 48 and 51. Onsets come from visible spectral renewals; gates are explicitly low-confidence estimates from the start of declining low-band envelopes. The excerpt stops before the fourth attack. No Septum output was used for transcription.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable; this is a source-audio reconstruction, not a recovered original performance.
All velocities are fixed to 100 as an explicit unknown placeholder; no velocity, preset parameter, or recording EQ was fitted to Septum output.

Played-note inference assumes default system transpose and the documented/current WIDE-dependent oscillator ranges. Original system settings, controller events, exact recorded patch revision, and recording processing are unknown.
Event times refer to decoded MP3 audio. Hardware latency, encoder history, oscillator state, and effect history are not recovered; no post-render alignment or time warping is implied.

The hardware attacks contain measurable pitch movement and the stable low sine is somewhat below equal temperament. No original pitch-bend/controller curve or master tune can be recovered, so none is invented in this note-only MIDI.

The published patch has long release and delay; note-off times are weak estimates (roughly ±100 ms), not measured key releases. Envelope shape differences must not be attributed solely to synthesizer fidelity.
Onset estimates have about 15–25 ms uncertainty; residual previous-note energy overlaps the next attack. The steady octave relation is stronger evidence than exact attack pitch or gates.
The final release continues beyond this 1.55-second crop and is not compared. The patch is kept unchanged, including its stored portamento-off value.
